text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: gpu-queue-growth (severity=high) — autoscaler reports max node limit reached. Root TS 1799999998
oncall-elena: I'm on it. joining now.
sre-raj: Got the alert. What's the current queue backlog?
oncall-elena: Prom query shows active inference queue ~12k requests, 95th latency spiking to 18s for hosted tier. Non-critical routes already throttling.
infra-mike: k8s autoscaler events: 
```
kubectl -n redwood get hpa,gpa
# HPA/GPA: no scale triggers, cluster-autoscaler event:
Events:
  Warning  ScaleUpFailed  cluster-autoscaler  Failed to scale up: reached max nodes in ASG (max: 120)
```
eng-runtime-chen: Logs from runtime: "AllocateGPU: insufficient resources: node capacity exhausted" repeated. We started evicting batch jobs but serving pods still pending.
ops-lead-ira: Any quick mitigation other than asking cloud for more nodes?
sre-raj: We can do emergency per-tenant rate limiting to reduce churn, and move large batch jobs to a lower priority queue. Patching config in 2 mins.
oncall-elena: @eng-runtime-chen can we fall back some routes to cpu-only cheaper models to keep latency bounded for small customers?
eng-runtime-chen: Yes — we have model-quantized variants. I can roll a canary redirect rule for non-SLA customers to model-x-small. Will take ~7m to rollout.
customer-success-anna: Heads-up: two enterprise customers in EU are seeing timeouts. Need a short customer-facing blurb. ETA on fix?
oncall-elena: Immediate mitigations: 1) apply rate limit to non-critical routes (2m) 2) redirect non-SLA traffic to quantized model (7m) 3) request manual node quota bump from cloud (IaaS) (TBD).
infra-mike: I raised a manual quota increase request with cloud console and infra-support (ticket #CLOUD-9482). They responded: "Request received — manual approval required, 30-45 min."
ops-lead-ira: 30-45 min is too long. Can we do a temporary capacity hack? e.g., double up on smaller GPU instances or add ephemeral nodes in a different ASG?
infra-mike: We have ephemeral ASG-spot-pool but autoscaler won't place GPUs there due to label mismatch. I can patch nodegroup selector to include spot pool for serving, but that risks preemption. Would you like me to do it?
sre-raj: Yes do it if we're accepting potential preemptions. We need immediate headroom.
eng-runtime-chen: Rolling patch to kube-scheduler tolerations + nodeSelector approach for serving pods. Will add toleration for spot-nodes, set lower priorityClass for non-critical pods so they can be preempted.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: Started deploy 0.0.12 -> infra/serve-routing (user: eng-runtime-chen)
eng-runtime-chen: Patching now — applying kustomize overlay: 
```
kubectl apply -f overlays/spot-fallback.yaml
# patch adds nodeSelector: gpu-type=any-spot and tolerations
```
eng-runtime-chen: Patch applied. New nodes requested. Cluster-autoscaler shows scale up events to spot-pool.
infra-mike: cloud ticket updated: PLR approved temporary quota increase (+20 nodes) — they asked for justification. I sent backlog graphs and an oncall pager link, got approval in 9 minutes.
oncall-elena: :thumbsup: Great. Can you link the approval doc?
infra-mike: https://console.cloud/requests/CLOUD-9482/approve (internal) — and IDM note: manual increase expires in 2 hours.
customer-success-anna: Drafting customer blurb: "We're experiencing higher-than-normal GPU demand which is causing increased latencies for some requests. We're actively scaling and routing lower-priority workloads to restore service. We'll update in 30 minutes." Any edits?
ops-lead-ira: Add: "No customer data was impacted. Enterprise customers with SLA will get priority and we are escalating capacity."
customer-success-anna: Updated. Posting to status page now.
eng-runtime-chen: Canary redirect rolled out to 40% traffic for non-SLA, rate limits applied to 3 low-priority routes. Queue length dropped from 12k -> 5.2k in 8 minutes. 95th latency down to 7s.
sre-raj: Good. Monitor for evictions. If spot nodes preempt we may see brief spikes. Also watch OOMKills — we lowered pod density on new nodes.
oncall-elena: Confirming: manual cloud quota gave us +20 nodes, spot-pool added ~10 ephemeral nodes, net headroom ~30 GPUs.
infra-mike: Affirmative. Cloud autoscaler now sees capacity and pending pods are scheduling.
incident-bot: incident recorded: INC-2026-314 (owner: oncall-elena)
ops-lead-ira: Postmortem actions to capture: - Hard cap alert threshold too permissive - runbook gap for spot-fallback labels - faster cloud approval escalation path - automated fallback to quantized models for non-SLA routes
sre-raj: I'm collecting metric snapshots and event timelines. Will paste Prom queries + grafana links to the ticket.
customer-success-anna: Status update posted to customers. ETA next update 30m or on resolution.
eng-runtime-chen: Final note: we should consider lowering default max_nodes for autoscaler to avoid sudden plateau illusions — and introduce warning to platform when cluster has <10% spare GPU headroom.
oncall-elena: Thanks team. Keep monitoring for 20m. If backlog doesn't drop below 500 in 30m we escalate to ops-lead.
infra-mike: Logged recovery actions and removed temporary toleration after the spot nodes stabilized. We'll keep manual quota active for 2hrs per approval.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (backlog < 300, latency normalizing). Closing thread.
ops-lead-ira: Great work. We'll convert this into a follow-up runbook and schedule a retro tomorrow. :coffee:
